name: security-llm-memory-tenancy-review
intent: Persistent agent memory ownership, retrieval and update authority
artifacts: Memory write API, namespace/identity keys, retrieval filters, summarization and deletion lifecycle.
trace: Trace who may persist or modify memory and which user/tenant receives it after later retrieval, including merged or summarized memories.
experiment: Use two owned actors with distinct synthetic memory markers; compare permitted recall and a controlled foreign namespace/update request.
disproof: A model recalling public shared knowledge is expected; similarity alone does not prove a specific private memory was retrieved.
repair: Bind memory writes/retrieval/retention to current actor authority and verify deletion and entitled recall.
branch_decisions: Resolve who owns a memory item and who may insert, update, retrieve or delete it. A shared team memory may intentionally cross individual accounts; compare against its declared audience. Follow stable tenant/user identifiers through retrieval filters, summarization and cache reuse, including account switching, rather than equating semantic similarity with an ownership grant.
operational_method: Retain provenance and permitted audience for each input item contributing to a summary or merged memory. The derived object audience must follow the declared intersection/declassification policy, not whichever namespace stores the summary. Compare a permitted team summary with one including a restricted synthetic item, then revoke/delete its source entitlement and inspect derived-memory reuse. A direct namespace filter alone does not establish derived-data isolation.
